match.reason: The bank card covers the V-shaped graph of y = |x| and absolute value as distance, but its main focus is solving |x − a| = b, and it does not teach the transformations the new point's brief mentions, so no bank point teaches the same idea closely enough to reuse or adapt.

draft.title: The absolute value function
card: The absolute value |x| is the distance of x from 0, so it is never negative. |x| = x when x ≥ 0, and |x| = −x when x < 0.
The graph of y = |x| is a V with its vertex at (0, 0). The part of y = x below the x-axis is reflected above it.
For y = |f(x)|, any part of the graph of f below the x-axis is reflected in the x-axis. Parts on or above the axis stay the same.
Transformations apply as usual. y = |x − 2| + 3 is a V with its vertex moved to (2, 3). Example: |−5| = 5 and |5| = 5.
draft.remember: Absolute value makes outputs non-negative by flipping any negative part upwards.

a.q: What is the vertex of the graph of y = |x + 1| − 4?
a.why: Inside the bars, x + 1 = 0 when x = −1, so the vertex has x = −1. The −4 outside moves the graph down 4, giving (−1, −4). The sign inside the bars shifts the graph the opposite way to what it looks like.
a.clue: Find the x-value that makes the inside zero.

b.q: The graph of y = x − 3 is reflected using y = |x − 3|. What is the y-intercept?
b.why: At x = 0, y = |0 − 3| = |−3| = 3. The value −3 is the y-intercept of y = x − 3, but the absolute value makes it positive.
b.clue: Substitute x = 0, then take the absolute value.
